title.value: Combining Modular Skills in Multitask Learning
title.justification: The title of the paper is stated explicitly at the beginning of the document as "Combining Modular Skills in Multitask Learning."
title.quote: Combining Modular Skills in Multitask Learning

extractions.description: This paper explores a modular design approach for neural networks, where a subset of latent discrete skills from a predetermined inventory is allocated to each task. This design aims to systematically improve generalization to new tasks by recombining autonomous facets of knowledge, resulting in sample efficiency in reinforcement learning and few-shot generalization in supervised learning.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on improving the efficiency and adaptability of machine learning models through a modular design. Although this may indirectly support sustainable development by optimizing resource use in AI systems, the paper does not specifically address any climate or ecological sustainable development goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: A modular design encourages neural models to disentangle and recombine different facets of knowledge to generalise more systematically to new tasks.

primary_category.justification: There is no direct or implied mention of climate or ecological sustainable development within the main themes of this paper.
primary_category.quote: The modular design of a network significantly increases sample-efficiency in reinforcement learning and few-shot generalisation in supervised learning, compared to baselines with fully shared, task-specific, or conditionally generated parameters where knowledge is entangled across tasks.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper lacks any secondary emphasis on climate or ecological sustainability aspects, focusing instead on neural network design and multitask learning.
secondary_categories.quote: We find that the modular design of a network significantly increases sample-efficiency in reinforcement learning and few-shot generalisation in supervised learning, compared to baselines with fully shared, task-specific, or conditionally generated parameters where knowledge is entangled across tasks.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-categories outlined within the climate and ecological sustainable development framework do not apply to the technical focus and scope of this paper.
primary_sub_category.quote: In both experiments, we surpass competitive baselines where parameters are fully shared, task-specific, combined according to expert knowledge, or generated conditionally on the task.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The technical innovations discussed in the paper are not related to any of the predefined sub-categories focused on sustainable development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Finally, we show that our model facilitates interpretability by learning an explicit hierarchy of tasks based on the skills they require.

applications.value: Sample efficiency in reinforcement learning and few-shot generalisation in supervised learning
applications.justification: The paper highlights applications that show improvements in machine learning model performance through modular design, leading to enhanced sample efficiency and better generalization in learning tasks.
applications.quote: We find that the modular design of a network significantly increases sample-efficiency in reinforcement learning and few-shot generalisation in supervised learning.

new_primary_category.justification: The themes explored in this paper do not introduce a new climate or ecological sustainable development category otherwise undefined in the existing framework.
new_primary_category.quote: In this work, we assume that each task is associated with a subset of latent discrete skills from a (potentially small) inventory.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper's research focus does not necessitate the creation of a new sub-category under the climate or ecological sustainable development categories.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: The proposed model is equivalent to performing a soft partition, represented by a binary matrix, of the set of skill-specific parameters.
